To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) DOC-2 is a new cardiac protein that is abundantly expressed in fibroblasts, 2) its expression is regulated by growth-promoting factors in cardiac fibroblast cultures, and 3) it is inversely related to collagen accumulation in the heart during chronic overload.
DOC-2 is abundantly expressed in cultured cardiac fibrobasts and that it is downregulated in the failing heart.

1) DOC-2 is a novel regulator of cardiac fibroblast growth and collagen synthesis, 2) the level of DOC-2 expression is inversely correlated with collagen expression during progression of hypertrophic remodeling in vivo, and 3) DOC-2 overexpression in cardiac fibroblast cultures leads to inhibition of ERK signaling and collagen expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of cardiac remodeling in the heart and the role of the adapter molecule DOC-2 in collagen expression.
the role of the adaptor molecule DOC-2 in heart hypertrophy.
the role of the adapter molecule DOC-2 in hemodynamic overload and its potential to inhibit collagen synthesis in cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of DOC- 2 is increased in volume-overloaded hearts and decreased in pressure-overloaded hearts.
the expression of the adapter molecule DOC-2, in cardiac fibroblast, is regulated by hemodynamic overloads.
DOC-2 expression is increased during cardiac hypertrophy and that it inhibits collagen production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DOC-2 is a negative regulator of cardiac fibroblast collagen expression.
DOC-2 is a potential regulator of the extracellular matrix in the heart.
the expression of DOC- 2 is increased in volume overload and inhibited in pressure overload, and that DOC- 2 inhibits collagen expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DOC-2 is an important molecule involved in cardiac remodeling.
DOC-2 may have a protective role in the development of cardiac fibrosis.
DOC-2 may play an important role in regulating collagen synthesis and may represent an important target for therapeutic intervention to prevent cardiac fibrosis.
